newsitem.title: GERMANY: German party maverick criticises Kohl candidacy.
newsitem.headline: German party maverick criticises Kohl candidacy.

text.p: A leading maverick in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's party has attacked Kohl's decision to stand for a fifth term in next year's election, German media reported on Saturday.
Kurt Biedenkopf, premier of Saxony state and long-time critic of Kohl, proposed a referendum of party members on the issue.

Biedenkopf told party general secretary Peter Hintze in a letter that Kohl's candidacy was a "particular risk" for the governing Christian Democrats (CDU), the daily Hannoversche Allgemeine Zeitung reported.

The weekly Focus said Biedenkopf had said at a CDU meeting last Monday that voters could be put off by the thought of extending even further Kohl's record tenure, which began in 1982. He said the party should seek a broader mandate for Kohl in the form of a referendum.
Kohl quickly dismissed Biedenkopf's criticism, telling a CDU regional conference in Trier that he had "recognised my duty" to stand again.
"I don't need coaching...from professors or anyone else," he said in a direct swipe at Biedenkopf, a former academic, prompting laughter from the floor.

Biedenkopf is the only leading CDU member to voice criticism since Kohl announced earlier this month that he would stand for a record fifth term. He was the only member of the leadership committee not to back Kohl's candidacy at Monday's meeting.

Kohl's declaration put an end to an unprecedented wave of public criticism above all from younger CDU politicians, and to suggestions that he might not have the stomach to tackle massive unemployment and necessary but unpopular structural reforms.
One of the up-and-coming CDU figures who dared earlier this year to criticise the government's performance under Kohl was quick to dismiss Biedenkopf's attack.

"Biedenkopf's behaviour is highly damaging to the party," Roland Koch, leader of the CDU in the Hesse regional assembly, told the weekly Bild am Sonntag. "He has started a pseudo-debate. If there were a party referendum Kohl would get 96 percent."
Labour Minister Norbert Bluem told the same paper that Biedenkopf, often ready to propose radical policies in defiance of the party line, was "not just an awkward thinker, but an intriguer".
Biedenkopf was one of a group of party liberals who tried to challenge Kohl's leadership at a CDU party conference in 1989.
In his letter to Hintze, Biedenkopf said that in the last four years under Kohl, the CDU had failed to carry out its promise to carry out structural reforms to make Germany fit for the next century.
He also challenged the argument that there was no real alternative to Kohl within the CDU.

To suggest this was equivalent to saying "that the CDU in its 24 years under Helmut Kohl's leadership has not managed to...prepare a new generation of politicians to take over the chancellor's leadership role", Biedenkopf said.
